blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jacob, also called Israel, had twelve sons. Joseph was seventeen, born when his father was old, and Jacob loved him more than all the others. Everyone in the family knew it.

verses.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours.
And when his brethren saw that their father loved him more than all his brethren, they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: A gift can be a blessing and a burden at once. Every time his brothers saw that coat, they saw what they had not been given. Then Joseph began to have dreams, and he told them.

verses.text: For, behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: His brothers hated him even more. Then he dreamed that the sun, the moon and eleven stars bowed down to him. Even his father scolded him for that one, but Jacob kept thinking about it.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: One day the brothers were far away with the flocks, and Jacob sent Joseph to check on them. He found them at Dothan. They saw him coming from a long way off, wearing that coat.

verses.text: And they said one to another, Behold, this dreamer cometh.
Come now therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into some pit, and we will say, Some evil beast hath devoured him: and we shall see what will become of his dreams.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Reuben, the oldest, spoke up. He told them not to kill Joseph, but to throw him into a pit in the wilderness instead. He meant to come back later, rescue him, and bring him home to their father.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when Joseph was come unto his brethren, that they stript Joseph out of his coat, his coat of many colours that was on him;
And they took him, and cast him into a pit: and the pit was empty, there was no water in it.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Then the brothers sat down to eat. Their brother was in a dry pit nearby, and they ate their meal. While they ate, they saw a group of Ishmeelites coming from Gilead, their camels loaded with spices on the way down to Egypt.

verses.text: And Judah said unto his brethren, What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?
Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother and our flesh. And his brethren were content.
Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Twenty pieces of silver. That was the price jealousy put on a brother. It is a hard story to sit with. But it does not end in that pit. Joseph was taken down to Egypt, and a little later the Bible tells us that the LORD was with Joseph there. The rest of his story is still to come.

first_reader.note: Drafted and read by Claude in the landing session; no free-model draft (QA_NO_FREE_MODEL not needed).

pastor.note: Faithful to Genesis 37 with 39:2 named as later; does not soften the brothers' sin.

cultural.note: The sale of a free person is told as the wrong it was; no servitude framing of Joseph's worth.
